Could AI build an executive-ready financial report from the same dataset you're using in Power BI?
Tomorrow we're going to find out. 

What happens when you combine six years of financial data from 100 S&P companies, Power BI, and AI?
Tomorrow's meetup is a live experiment.

Andrej Lapajne , founder of Zebra BI, and Rich Cooper , CEO of Zebra BI, will take a benchmark dataset built from public financial statements across six industries and put it through its paces.
You'll see:
• Financial reporting in Power BI using IBCS-standard visualisations
• Dynamic benchmarking across companies such as Nike and Adidas
• KPIs, variance analysis, multi-currency reporting and executive dashboards
• How AI can generate executive-ready financial narratives and P&L waterfalls directly from the same dataset
The interesting part isn't Power BI versus AI.
It's seeing how they complement each other.
One provides structure, consistency and trust in the numbers. The other accelerates insight, storytelling and decision-making.
No slide deck. Just live demonstrations, real data and plenty of opportunities for questions.
Looking forward to seeing where the discussion takes us.

🎨 Apparently accessibility “isn’t technical enough”… so after using UDFs for alternative text, I built my own colour contrast ratio checker in Power BI! 😄

I talk about accessibility all the time, especially colour contrast. Yet somehow, people still think it’s “not that technical” or “that’s just design fluff.” So I set out to prove them wrong.

The result? A fully dynamic Power BI colour contrast ratio checker powered purely by DAX, translating the actual WCAG luminance formula into Power BI logic.

This meant:
🔹 Converting HEX into RGB channels
🔹 Applying the gamma‑corrected relative luminance formula
🔹 Calculating contrast ratios the way WCAG intended
🔹 And letting Power BI pass show you if you are compliant

Just serious DAX, serious maths, and a surprising amount of time spent questioning why the colour “chocolate” looks aggressively orange 🍊😅. And guess what? I’ve also packaged the luminance logic into a reusable DAX UDF, which I’ll be sharing. So next time you’re building a report, there’s officially no excuse for guessing your colour contrast instead of testing it.

And now?
Well… maybe this will finally make me sound more technical?!
(A girl can dream 😄)

Jokes aside, I’m going to post the solution and UDF on my blog, so watch this space! 👀✨

🚨🚨More on Accessibility?🚨🚨
Join me at WCAG Compliance in Power BI: Making Data Accessible to All hosted by Sue Bayes.

The output is the actual contrast ratio and the Pass/Fail status for WCAG AA (regular and large text and non-text) and WCAG AAA (regular and large text)

items.content:
You already know who it is.

Don't bother naming them. 

It's you. Not because you're slow. 

It's that you walk out of meetings, sure you'll remember the three things that mattered, and by your desk, you've got one.

The dumbest person in the meeting is the one still running on memory. That's the figuring out.

Here's how you stop being the dumbest one:

1. Download Granola .ai. It's an Apple-style notepad, not a bot - nothing joins your call. It just listens and writes the notes while you nod.

2. Connect it to Claude as a connector: 
Settings → Connectors → Granola.

3. Teach Claude your writing style (once): 
"Read my last 30 sent emails. Write my voice profile - how I greet, sign off, my go-to phrases, what I never say." 

Save it. (Skip this & your follow-ups sound like a robot that just learned "circle back.")

4. After any meeting, one prompt in Claude: "Pull my last meeting from Granola. Draft the follow-up in my voice - decisions, action items with owners, next step. Make it a draft."

items.content:
Claude is useless until you do this. 

7 connectors worth turning on (with exact prompts):

Step 1. Open Claude.
Step 2. Click the '+' inside the chatbox.
Step 3. Hit 'Connectors' → 'Add connector.'

Now turn these 7 on (+ prompts to use for each):

Connector 1. Granola.
Turn meetings into action, not notes.
Prompt: "Pull my last Granola meeting. Summarize in 5 bullets. List my action items with deadlines & flag 2-5 blockers."

(download granola .ai first & open it in the background while having calls to get meeting notes)

Connector 2. Gmail.
Clear your inbox without reading it.
Prompt: "Read my Gmail this week. Bucket every email into: reply today, reply Friday, ignore. Save urgent replies as drafts."

Connector 3. Slack.
Skip the noise. Catch what matters.
Prompt: "Read my key channels from the last 48 hours. Surface the 3 things I need to react to. Skip jokes & standups."

Connector 4. Notion.
Reuse what worked. Stop starting from scratch.
Prompt: "Open my content calendar. Pull last week's posts. Create 2 new ones in the same tone. Save back to Notion as drafts."

Connector 5. Google Drive.
Spreadsheets in minutes, not hours.
Prompt: "In Cowork, build a spreadsheet for [topic] from my uploaded files. Push the final version to Drive as a Google Sheet."

Connector 6. Gamma.
Prompt → full deck.
Prompt: "Create a 10-slide deck on [topic] for [audience]. Cover the 5 key points below. One idea per slide."

Connector 7. Combine them.
What 99% of people miss.
Prompt: "Read my last Granola meeting, the related Slack thread & any Gmail follow-ups. Give me a 1-page brief: decided, pending, who owes what."

✦ Here's why most people never use connectors:
"I'll paste the Slack thread in real quick."
"I'll find that Drive doc & copy it over."
"I'll re-summarize the meeting from memory."

5 minutes per task. 50 tasks per week.
4 hours gone. Every single week.

That's like having an assistant & never telling them where the files are. The assistant is smart. You're just doing their job for them.
